newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK activists warn Japan to back down over isles.
newsitem.headline: HK activists warn Japan to back down over isles.

text.p: Hong Kong activists who support China's claim to a group of East China Sea islets on Friday gave Japan a deadline to back down from its claim or face a fresh landing attempt on the isles.

"We are now giving the Japan government two and a half months to tear down all structures on the islands signifying its claims and discuss with the Chinese government on the issue," Lew Mon Hung, an organiser of the Bao Diao Ho Patriotic Movement Committee said at a news conference.
"If the Japanese government doesn't do so by March 28, we will sail to the islands," Lew told reporters.

If Tokyo refuses to comply, the activists plan to camp for up to a week on the isles, known as the Diaoyus in Chinese and Senkakus in Japanese, and tear down Japanese flags and a makeshift lighthouse.
They also plan to erect monuments signifying China's claim.
"The revival of Japanese militarism has escalated to such an alarming level, we just can't sit by," activist Chen Yu Shu told reporters.
The group's plan follows fury in Hong Kong, Taiwan and China last September after an ultra-rightist Japanese group erected a lighthouse on one of the islands.
The outrage came to a boil when Hong Kong activist David Chan drowned after he jumped off a boat near the isles in defiance of Japanese claims to the islands.

The activists, who have invited other Chinese nationalist groups to participate in the landing attempt, said they would charter a vessel to be skippered by Ngai Lup-chee, the same man who captained the voyage on which Chan died.
The activists, who hope to bring 80 people for the planned voyage in March, half of them journalists, also want to erect a monument in honour of Chan.
